lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD $33 / 1.22 = $27.05, round down to $25 hammer ($30.50 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $40 (top of the close Gowans pairs), less about 15% seller commission and no postage (local auction resale) = $34; $34 / 2.44 = $13.93, round down to $10. Comparables are lighter or plainer than this pair, so these are conservative.
lots.confidence_reason: Hallmarks visible but not legible, weight not stated, and the 2 close SOLD comparables are only from Gowans API data (no separate lot pages) and differ in form. WebSearch was capped, so no Armitage past results, UK results or retail checks were possible.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 5 researcher entries confirmed in the Gowans API (ids, prices, bid counts, dates match). Three re-filed as category guide only. Lot id 380473 added for the ladle and salt entry.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Embossed floral and C-scroll repousse with vacant cartouche on each side, flared oval rims, gilt or gilt-washed interiors, oval foot. A row of small hallmark punches on the rim of each salt; enlarged crops show punch outlines but no readable lion, town mark or date letter. No obvious splits or dents visible; light surface wear.
lots.condition: Appears good, light wear, no visible splits or repairs in the photos. Gilding to interiors looks intact. Marks not readable.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the hallmarks (lion passant, town mark, date letter, maker) and give the combined weight in grams? Any splits, holes or repairs in the embossed bodies?

lots.what_it_is: Green glass oval dish with intaglio-moulded scene of two cherubs or putti, set in a gilt-metal filigree mount with red and blue paste cabochons, two scroll handles and four feet. Typical of Czech (Bohemian) jewelled filigree dressing-table ware of the 1920s to 1930s. Green with a yellow edge tint; uranium content unconfirmed (needs a UV torch). No mark seen.
lots.score_reason: An attractive and decorative piece, but no same-item or close comparable was found. The only local evidence is plain green and uranium glass at $45 to $75 hammer and a Josef Inwald green glass bowl at $170. Likely $50 to $150; evidence is too thin to support a bid.

lots.what_it_is: Mixed group of unnamed WWII and later medals: two 1939-45 Stars on ribbon, a Burma Star on ribbon, a GVI Defence Medal on ribbon, a further unribboned star (likely Africa Star, with a loose Africa Star ribbon), a US Antarctica Service Medal with Wintered Over bar plus its ribbon bar, a US Air Force Good Conduct Medal, and a Queen Elizabeth II commemorative medallion (arms reverse, possibly a 1953 coronation or royal visit piece) on a blue pin ribbon.
lots.score_reason: Researcher's identification of the US pieces was wrong: the COURAGE SACRIFICE DEVOTION medal is a US Antarctica Service Medal with Wintered Over bar, and the eagle medal is an Air Force Good Conduct Medal. Unnamed single WWII medals make $35 to $40 hammer at Gowans, so 5 British pieces plus the Antarctic medal could reasonably reach $150 to $250 if genuine. But no matching group sale was found, and replica stars are common.

lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos (front and back). Stars have the GRI VI cypher and correct ribbons: 2 x 1939-45 Star (dark blue, red, light blue), 1 x Burma Star (dark blue with orange and red). Defence Medal with uncrowned GVI bust obverse and green and orange ribbon. One loose star with ring, reverse unclear. Loose Africa Star ribbon. US Antarctica Service Medal: hooded figure obverse, COURAGE SACRIFICE DEVOTION over polar map reverse, Wintered Over bar on ribbon, plus ribbon bar. US Air Force Good Conduct Medal: eagle on sword and book with EFFICIENCY HONOR FIDELITY. QEII crowned bust medallion with arms reverse on blue ribbon with pin. British WWII stars were issued unnamed; no reverse naming visible.
lots.condition: Fair to good; ribbons a bit faded and frayed, medals with normal toning. Authenticity of stars unconfirmed (copies are common).
lots.question_for_armitage: Are any of the medals named or numbered (check reverse of stars and the Defence Medal rim, Australian issues were impressed)? Do the stars look like originals (weight, crisp detail, flat reverse) rather than copies? Which star is the unribboned one?
